She had been playing on the phone, and after a hard day of bicycling around the cul de sac, rolling down steep hills, and killing imaginary aliens with friends (seriously, they were called Dramatoids), I walk into our garage-turned-playroom ready to plop in front of our old tube TV and watch cartoons, but before I can turn the TV on, she giggles and hands me the phone.

"Look how cool it is! Look, you can even call 911 without pressing the "On" button on the phone. Don't worry, it won't go through."

So I do just that, and then our phone rings. I answer the phone and I get the dispatcher spiel and hang up immediately which, naturally, prompts them to call back. Repeat a couple of times and finally I admit that I was playing with the phone and they send a pair of cops over to our house to verify that everything is OK.

When they arrive, I start bawling and apologizing, barely able to force the words "I thought it was off," through tears and snot and stupid sobs. They warn me how 911 should only be used for emergencies and they go on their merry ways (without fining my parents, thankfully). For 22 years I believed that the phone had a silent dial or some kind of callback feature. A couple of months ago, somewhere between beer and whiskey, my sister revealed to me that she had called the cops with the phone on, and that my timing was too perfect for her to not pass the buck.
